recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Further changes to Observation.category cardinality, binding strength, or categorization guidance should wait for a new OO work-group decision because the current source reflects FHIR-11113 together with the related FHIR-9543 and FHIR-9857 decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-11113 was a Published FHIR-core Observation issue resolved Not Persuasive with Modification. It objected to making Observation.category too unbounded after the 0..* cardinality change and approved clarification that category supports search/indexing schemes and multiple categories rather than reverting the cardinality.
initial_application: No current combined-branch reconciliation commit existed and no source-history commit explicitly mentioned FHIR-11113. Git history shows commit bd736a46cc changed the Observation.category spreadsheet comment from the older multiple-axis wording to the FHIR-11113 approved clarification, though its subject referenced neighboring tracker #11115; the 2021 source refactor carried that text into structuredefinition-Observation.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-9543 approved changing Observation.category from 0..1 to 0..* and requested descriptive clarification. FHIR-9857 later approved preferred binding for Observation.category because a stronger binding would require every repeated CodeableConcept to contain a value-set code. No directly relevant Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that conflicts with the Jira/source conclusion.

Observation is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, and source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml already has max="*", a preferred ObservationCategory binding, and the approved comment allowing owner-defined categorization schemes and multiple categories.
